raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Shared KV-event consumers reject SGLang `BlockStored` messages because the required nullable `lora_name` field is missing. Consumers that derive salted cache keys from `extra_keys` also cannot find SGLang's salt there.

This draft contains an implementation of **proposed Phase 1 of #39991**. Replay framing and LoRA adapter-name/hash propagation remain separate follow-ups, so this PR does not close the RFC.

## Modifications

- Always serialize nullable `medium` and `lora_name`; producers emit `lora_name=None`.
- Emit the cache salt in `extra_keys` only for block zero of a full prefix. Keep entries aligned with `block_hashes` when stores coalesce, including padding absent entries. Preserve the named `cache_salt` and `session_id` fields.
- Apply the same metadata rule to the Rust adapter using its existing parent hash, block count, and salt. No Rust binding tuple or native implementation change is needed.
- Document the wire metadata and add registered CPU regression tests for required nulls, legacy decoders, coalescing, prefix continuations, and Python/Rust parity after extension and node splitting.

A separate commit relocates the unchanged MXFP8 reserved-slot test added by #35351 from `test/registered/kernel/quantization/` to `test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/`. The latest upstream commit otherwise fails the repository's registered-test taxonomy check; the failure was reproduced on unmodified `main`. This is a path-only correction with no test-content changes.

Block hashes, storage-tier names, batch layout, and transport framing are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output changes. Validation used local Linux ARM64 CPU execution with the real compiled Rust extension, Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.13.0, and msgspec 0.21.1:

```bash
python -m pytest --noconftest \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_kv_events.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_cache_events.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_unit.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_rust_tree_core_integration.py \
  -k 'not test_memory_allocated' -q -rs -p no:cacheprovider
```

Result: **173 passed, 1 skipped, 1 deselected; 89 subtests passed**. The skipped test requires CUDA. The existing `test_memory_allocated` is deselected because it calls `torch.get_device_module().memory_allocated()`, which is unavailable on CPU.

The CPU suite, changed-line coverage, and full pre-commit checks were rerun after rebasing onto `main` at `0cb37c018c`. All passed after the path-only test relocation described above.

Additional checks:

- The same suite passed with `--cov --cov-config=.coveragerc --cov-report=xml`. `diff-cover coverage.xml --compare-branch=origin/main --fail-under=60` reported **100% of changed executable lines covered (13/13)**.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` passed with the repository's Rust toolchains.
- `mint@4.2.559 validate` and `mint@4.2.559 broken-links --check-anchors --check-redirects` passed.
- `node docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference-speed claim. This changes opt-in event metadata and does not modify model execution, kernels, or scheduling. No GPU inference benchmark was run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add registered regression tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide relevant validation; model accuracy and GPU speed benchmarks are not applicable to this metadata change.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

## Review and Merge Process

This PR is on hold as a draft pending maintainer agreement on #39991, following the [issue author's clarification](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39991#issuecomment-5779276096). The implementation and validation results are preserved for reference. Further implementation updates and CI requests are paused until the RFC scope is agreed.

+"""CPU coverage for per-block namespace metadata in KV placement events."""
+
+import unittest
+from array import array
+
+import msgspec
+
+from sglang.srt.disaggregation.kv_events import BlockStored, StorageMedium
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.events import KVCacheEventRecorder, cache_salt_extra_keys
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.radix_cache import RadixKey, TreeNode
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=3, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestKVCacheEventMetadata(CustomTestCase):
+    @staticmethod
+    def _node(tokens, *, salt=None, parent=None):
+        if parent is None:
+            parent = TreeNode()
+            parent.key = RadixKey(array("q"))
+            parent.hash_value = []
+        node = TreeNode()
+        node.parent = parent
+        node.key = RadixKey(array("q", tokens), cache_salt=salt)
+        return node
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _store(hashes, *, parent=None, extras=None, salt="tenant-a", lora_name=None):
+        return BlockStored(
+            block_hashes=hashes,
+            parent_block_hash=parent,
+            token_ids=[1, 2] * len(hashes),
+            block_size=2,
+            lora_id=None,
+            medium=StorageMedium.GPU,
+            lora_name=lora_name,
+            extra_keys=extras,
+            cache_salt=salt,
+        )
+
+    def test_salt_only_appears_on_the_first_block_of_the_prefix(self):
+        for medium in (StorageMedium.GPU, StorageMedium.CPU):
+            with self.subTest(medium=medium):
+                recorder = KVCacheEventRecorder(enabled=True, page_size=2)
+                first = self._node([1, 2, 3, 4], salt="tenant-a")
+                recorder.record_store(first, medium=medium)
+                event = recorder.take()[0]
+                self.assertEqual(event.extra_keys, [("tenant-a",), None])
+                self.assertEqual(len(event.extra_keys), len(event.block_hashes))
+                self.assertEqual(event.cache_salt, "tenant-a")
+                self.assertIsNone(event.lora_name)
+
+                child = self._node([5, 6, 7, 8], salt="tenant-a", parent=first)
+                recorder.record_store(child, medium=medium)
+                continuation = recorder.take()[0]
+                self.assertEqual(continuation.parent_block_hash, event.block_hashes[-1])
+                self.assertIsNone(continuation.extra_keys)
+                self.assertEqual(continuation.cache_salt, "tenant-a")
+
+    def test_partial_blocks_keep_extras_aligned(self):
+        recorder = KVCacheEventRecorder(enabled=True, page_size=2)
+        recorder.record_store(self._node([1, 2, 3], salt="tenant-a"))
+        events = recorder.take()
+        self.assertEqual([e.block_size for e in events], [2, 1])
+        self.assertEqual(events[0].extra_keys, [("tenant-a",)])
+        self.assertIsNone(events[1].extra_keys)
+        self.assertEqual(events[1].parent_block_hash, events[0].block_hashes[-1])
+
+    def test_unsalted_events_omit_extra_keys(self):
+        recorder = KVCacheEventRecorder(enabled=True, page_size=2)
+        recorder.record_store(self._node([1, 2, 3, 4]))
+        event = recorder.take()[0]
+        self.assertIsNone(event.extra_keys)
+        wire = msgspec.msgpack.decode(msgspec.msgpack.encode(event))
+        self.assertNotIn("extra_keys", wire)
+        self.assertNotIn("cache_salt", wire)
+
+    def test_merge_extends_extras_with_a_placeholder_for_each_block(self):
+        recorder = KVCacheEventRecorder(enabled=True, page_size=2)
+        recorder.enqueue(self._store([1], extras=[("tenant-a",)]))
+        recorder.enqueue(self._store([2, 3], parent=1))
+        event = recorder.take()[0]
+        self.assertEqual(event.block_hashes, [1, 2, 3])
+        self.assertEqual(event.extra_keys, [("tenant-a",), None, None])
+
+    def test_merge_preserves_incoming_extras_and_backfills_missing_entries(self):
+        recorder = KVCacheEventRecorder(enabled=True, page_size=2)
+        recorder.enqueue(self._store([1, 2]))
+        recorder.enqueue(self._store([3], parent=2, extras=[("metadata",)]))
+        event = recorder.take()[0]
+        self.assertEqual(event.block_hashes, [1, 2, 3])
+        self.assertEqual(event.extra_keys, [None, None, ("metadata",)])
+
+    def test_different_salts_and_lora_names_are_not_merged(self):
+        for incoming in (
+            self._store([2], parent=1, salt="tenant-b"),
+            self._store([2], parent=1, lora_name="adapter-a"),
+        ):
+            recorder = KVCacheEventRecorder(enabled=True, page_size=2)
+            recorder.enqueue(self._store([1], extras=[("tenant-a",)]))
+            recorder.enqueue(incoming)
+            self.assertEqual(len(recorder.take()), 2)
+
+    def test_root_metadata_handles_empty_and_unicode_salts(self):
+        cases = [
+            (None, None, 2, None),
+            (None, "", 2, None),
+            (None, "tenant-a", 0, None),
+            (0, "tenant-a", 2, None),
+            (None, "tenant-\u03b1", 2, [("tenant-\u03b1",), None]),
+        ]
+        for parent, salt, count, expected in cases:
+            with self.subTest(parent=parent, salt=salt, count=count):
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    cache_salt_extra_keys(
+                        parent_block_hash=parent, cache_salt=salt, num_blocks=count
+                    ),
+                    expected,
+                )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

             block_size=block_size,

@@ -781,6 +782,7 @@ def test_cache_salt_is_included_in_store_and_remove_events(self):
 
         self.assertEqual(len(stored), 1)

issue_comments.body:
Update: I have moved this PR back to draft while maintainers discuss #39991, following the [issue author's clarification](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39991#issuecomment-5779276096). Please disregard my earlier request to start implementation review and CI until the RFC has maintainer agreement.

The implementation and local validation results are preserved: 173 tests passed, changed-line coverage was 100%, and pre-commit passed on the recorded base. The two GPU-dependent cases remain untested locally, as documented in the PR.

Thanks @PansaLegrand. Closing this because you have 9 PRs open and none updated in 7 days, over our soft cap of 5 for idle PRs.

Reopen the two or three you most want reviewed - a short active set moves faster than a long idle one.

Some directories moved recently, so an older branch may need retargeting:
`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.
